observable_outcome: The environment a child process receives has exactly one authority, and the type system enforces it. provider.Invocation loses its Environment field, and with it internal/runner's Grant.Apply and ProviderClient.Grant, because the field was written by one function whose one caller is never given the input that triggers it and was read only by a fake -- so no value it carried ever reached a process. What replaces it is not a second channel but a refusal: SupervisedInvocationRunner.Run, which already builds the child's environment from the approved provider-preflight record's base names and hands it to a supervisor that REPLACES rather than extends the parent environment, now refuses fail-closed -- after loading the record and strictly before debiting any ledger reservation -- when that record declares an environment.granted_names it has no channel to deliver. A declaration the runner cannot honour therefore stops the invocation instead of being silently dropped. V2-077's landed guard test keeps its name and is generalised from 'Run does not read Environment' into the class guard 'provider.Invocation declares no field that Run does not consume', so the next field of this shape turns a test red the day it is added rather than three live exercises later. This task closes a latent defect and no open hole: no non-test file constructs a Secret Broker, no file sets ProviderClient.Grant, every approved record declares granted_names empty, and the contracts layer forbids a non-empty one for the only provider any record names.
acceptance_criteria: A1. Scope boundary, written into the evidence before any code is edited, as a table with one row each. (1) What this task makes true: the environment a child receives has exactly one authority, enforced by the absence of any other field to carry one, and a record that declares an undeliverable grant refuses the invocation. (2) What it deliberately does not do: it does not widen what any child may reach, it adds no new environment entry, it delivers no credential to any child, it changes no mount, it changes no argv, and it changes the bytes a real claude child receives not at all. (3) What it records but does not fix: SupervisedInvocationRunner.ExtraEnv as the one declared additive source outside the record, and Grant.id as a field nothing reads (dp-v2-078 d11). (4) What only a later task can establish: actual delivery of a granted name to a child, in the shape dp-v2-078 d7 names, with its own credential-isolation acceptance. (5) That this task closes a LATENT defect and no open hole, in those words, with A3's measurements as the proof. (6) That this task passes no release gate and satisfies no M6 completion condition.
